misconceptions.description: Treating a vendor percentage or statistic as evidence without the comparison group, measure, sample, or funding source
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites a vendor figure as proof without asking what it was measured against
misconceptions.feedback: Ask what the number compares to, how it was measured, on how many learners, and who funded it. A bare figure is a claim, not evidence.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a peer-reviewed label removes a conflict of interest or a too-small sample
misconceptions.trigger: learner gives full weight to a vendor-funded study because it is peer reviewed
misconceptions.feedback: Peer review does not erase a funding conflict or a tiny sample. Weight the source by independence and sample size, not the label alone.

misconceptions.description: Treating an AI summary of vendor claims as independent verification of those claims
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts an AI 'fact-check' that may echo the vendor's own framing
misconceptions.feedback: An AI may repeat the vendor's framing. Use it to find primary sources, then verify each claim against a source you can read yourself.

misconceptions.description: Reading an engagement or time-on-task gain as evidence of learning gains
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites an engagement metric to justify a learning claim
misconceptions.feedback: Engagement is a proxy that can rise without learning rising. Ask for a learning measure tied to the instructional goal.
